claims.title: Stock Buybacks Are Theft From Workers
claims.socialistClaimText: Share buybacks are pure financial engineering that steal cash workers produced and should have received as wages or public investment. Ban buybacks and force reinvestment or redistribution.
claims.executiveSummary: Buybacks return capital to owners when firms lack higher-return projects - economically similar to dividends with tax and flexibility differences. Banning them does not magically raise wages; wages track productivity, labor markets, and firm-specific human capital. Forcing trapped cash into low-return projects wastes capital and slows growth that funds real wage gains.
evidenceBullets: SEC rules permit buybacks under disclosure frameworks; they are not 'stealing' in the legal or accounting sense of diverting employee escrow.
BEA / BLS productivity and real compensation series: long-run real wage growth tracks productivity more closely than short-run buyback waves.
When buybacks are restricted, firms may increase dividends, M&A, or low-NPV empire building rather than across-the-board raises.
Capital reallocation to higher-valued uses (including new startups that hire) is a feature of open capital markets, not a bug.

claims.title: Price-Gouging Bans Protect Consumers After Disasters
claims.socialistClaimText: After hurricanes and emergencies, sellers must not raise prices - 'gouging' is exploitation. Strict caps and prosecutions keep essentials affordable for working people.
claims.executiveSummary: Emergency price spikes are ugly but allocate scarce goods, attract truckers and inventories, and discourage hoarding. Caps create empty shelves, queues, and black markets - the same shortage pattern as peacetime price controls. Targeted aid (cash, vouchers) helps the poor without destroying the price signal that restores supply.
evidenceBullets: Basic supply-and-demand: when demand jumps and supply is disrupted, the market-clearing price rises; preventing that rise rations by waiting, favoritism, or force.
Historical disaster case studies and economics literature show faster restocking where prices can adjust versus prolonged shortages under caps.
BLS CPI and regional price data spike temporarily after supply shocks, then normalize as logistics recover - not as permanent 'greed' levels.
Means-tested emergency transfers preserve incentives for distant suppliers to divert inventory toward the crisis zone.

claims.title: Nationalize Energy, Rail, and Critical Infrastructure
claims.socialistClaimText: Private ownership of energy grids, rail, and 'critical infrastructure' puts profit over people. Public ownership guarantees reliability, equity, and climate goals.
claims.executiveSummary: Public ownership can solve some network externalities, but it also concentrates political risk, soft budget constraints, and underinvestment. Mixed systems with regulated private capital, open access rules, and transparent pricing have stronger maintenance and innovation records than fully nationalized sectors that treated infrastructure as a patronage machine.
evidenceBullets: EIA and DOE data show U.S. private and mixed energy investment cycles responding to prices and regulation - nationalization does not eliminate scarcity of capital or fuel.
Historical nationalized rail and heavy industry in socialist and mid-century systems often ran chronic losses, deferred maintenance, and political pricing.
Reliability metrics (outages, on-time performance) depend on incentives and capital budgeting more than the word 'public' on the letterhead.
Climate goals need cost-effective abatement signals; state monopolies can hide costs off-budget rather than reveal them.

claims.title: Universal Free Childcare Is a Basic Right
claims.socialistClaimText: Childcare is a public good and feminist necessity. Universal free government childcare should replace market provision that prices out working families.
claims.executiveSummary: High childcare costs are a real burden, driven by labor intensity, regulation, and local supply constraints. Universal free provision shifts costs onto taxes and queues; it does not abolish scarcity of caregivers. Targeted subsidies, zoning reform for home-based care, and labor-market flexibility expand access without creating a single state monopoly over early childhood.
evidenceBullets: BLS Consumer Expenditure and employment data show childcare as a major budget item for young families - the problem is real.
CBO and state budget analyses: universal free programs have large fiscal costs that compete with other priorities and require tax or deficit finance.
Supply constraints (staffing ratios, licensing, facility rules) limit scale; removing only the price signal without expanding supply creates rationing.
Nordic models pair subsidies with high taxes and labor-force institutions - not free of trade-offs or private/cooperative provision.

claims.title: Housing Must Be Decommodified
claims.socialistClaimText: Housing is a human right, not a commodity. Markets and landlords should be replaced by social housing, decommodification, and strict limits on private rental profit.
claims.executiveSummary: Treating housing only as a right without a supply plan produces queues and political allocation. High prices in superstar cities track zoning, permitting delays, and demand - not a moral failure of 'commodification' alone. Expanding legal supply, reducing exclusionary zoning, and targeted vouchers beat blanket decommodification that freezes construction and mobility.
evidenceBullets: Census and HUD housing data: shortage of units where demand is highest correlates with tight land-use regulation.
Rent control and decommodification experiments reduce turnover and new supply incentives (see also 2020s rent-control claim evidence).
Social housing succeeds when paired with ongoing construction finance; it fails when treated as a permanent price freeze without building.
Homeownership and private rental markets expanded middle-class housing stock historically; abolishing market signals reintroduces waiting lists.

claims.title: Corporate Personhood Destroys Democracy
claims.socialistClaimText: Treating corporations as persons lets capital drown out citizens. Abolish corporate personhood and corporate speech rights so democracy can serve people, not profit.
claims.executiveSummary: Corporate legal personality is a liability and contracting tool that lets people pool capital, sue, and be sued without unlimited personal risk for every investor. Removing it would not magically equalize speech; large unions, NGOs, and media firms would still organize. The Founding-era answer to concentrated power is competing centers of power, free speech, and limited government - not selective speech bans by entity type.
evidenceBullets: Corporate charters and limited liability historically expanded investment and middle-class equity ownership (Census SCF / Fed wealth data context).
Supreme Court corporate speech cases sit inside a broader First Amendment tradition protecting associations, not only natural persons.
Campaign finance and lobbying problems are better addressed with transparent disclosure and limits that apply neutrally than by dissolving business entities.
State-owned enterprises and party-controlled firms in socialist systems spent heavily on propaganda without 'corporate personhood' as Americans know it.

claims.title: Mandate Worker Ownership of All Firms
claims.socialistClaimText: True economic democracy requires mandatory worker ownership or board control of every firm. Capitalist equity is illegitimate hierarchy over labor.
claims.executiveSummary: Worker cooperatives can be excellent voluntary firms and deserve a level legal field. Mandating them for all enterprise destroys residual claimancy diversity, raises capital costs, and blocks outside investment that scales production. Successful co-ops still face market prices, bankruptcy, and the calculation problem; coercion does not remove trade-offs.
evidenceBullets: BLS business employment dynamics: most job creation comes from firms that need outside capital to grow - pure internal labor equity constrains scale.
Historical mandatory socialization experiments redistributed control to parties and managers more often than to shop-floor workers.
ESOPs and voluntary co-ops already exist in market economies; mandating one residual-claimant form bans competing governance experiments.
Public choice: mandatory worker boards become political arenas for factional control rather than automatic harmony.
